Hello! I'm Beau! I'm a very sweet boy with a unique feature. I'm a tripod! But don't let that fool you, I'm even more playful as ever! I love to go on walks and be outside. I even enjoy the water! I am house and kennel trained, and I love to hang out with the other dogs in my foster home. Sometimes we will play, but we all like to relax together too! While I get along with the dogs in my foster home, I do need slower intros with other dogs to help me feel comfortable. I am not a fan of hissing cats, so a home without cats would be best.

I enjoy puzzle toys and dog safe chews.  While I am a playful and adventerous boy, I also like to snuggle sometimes. Apartment life is too overwhelming for me, so I need a house, preferably with a fenced in yard, to call my forever home. However, the fenced in yard is not a dealbreaker since I enjoy going on walks.

I do have anxiety and allergies, so I take meds for them. But don't worry, I do really well taking them!

Are you my perfect match?

211913939.description:
Hi, I’m Pepper! 🐾

I’m an 8 ½ year-old bundle of love with the biggest heart and so much love to give! My foster family says I’m a special girl with a goofy personality, a playful spirit, and a heart that is truly one of a kind.

I may need a little extra patience and understanding when getting to know new people and navigating the world around me. New experiences and unfamiliar dogs can sometimes feel overwhelming, so I’m looking for someone who understands that building trust is a process. I may not open my heart overnight, but when I do, you’ll have a friend who loves with her whole heart. Once I trust you, you’ll get to see the real Pepper - the silly, affectionate, playful girl who loves to snuggle, give kisses, lean in for affection, and make you laugh. I have so much personality packed into this big body, and I truly believe I’m a lap dog! My favorite things include toys, treats, naps, and spending time with my people. And yes, my adorable snoring is just one of my many charms!

I currently live with another female dog, and we have a wonderful relationship. We love to play and chase each other, and she is a very special part of my world. While I do well with my resident dog, I have found that I’m most comfortable in a home where I don’t have to share my people or space with other dogs. I would likely thrive as the only dog in the home, where I can soak up all the love and attention. I’m looking for a quieter home with a patient, compassionate person or family who understands my needs and will give me the time and support I deserve. A female-led home would be a wonderful fit for me, and I would do best without children. I’m hoping for someone who sees the beauty in taking things slowly and understands that the most meaningful relationships are built one day at a time.

My foster family has watched me come so far. I’m learning that the world can be a wonderful place and that new experiences don’t always have to be scary. Every little bit of progress makes us so proud, and we know there is still so much happiness ahead of me. I’m a playful, loving girl who has so much more to discover. I may need someone willing to be patient, but I promise that the love I give in return is worth every moment. Once you become my person, you’ll have a loyal companion who wants nothing more than to be by your side. My foster family loves me dearly, and while saying goodbye will be incredibly difficult, they know there is someone out there who will see just how extraordinary I am.

I’m not looking for a perfect home. I’m looking for the right home - a home with patience, understanding, and a whole lot of heart. If you’re willing to give me the time I need to feel safe and loved, I’ll show you just how much love this big-hearted girl has to give ❤️

212359159.description:
Sweet Maple has been with us since she was 4-weeks-old. She came in with her mom (pictured with her) and 6 siblings, who have all be long since adopted. For some reason Maple sits and waits.

She started out going to the same events as her siblings, and got no interest. She was posted online everywhere, and got no interest.

We stopped attending events due to Maple being very shut down at them. We tried again once she was old enough to be on leash and outdoor events started; however, she was still very anxious and had a really hard time warming up to people.

Maple at home is an entirely different story. She warms up to people so fast, especially if you have treats, and a doggie friend for her to play with.

Maple is a very cautious girl, around people and will require another dog in the home for her to buddy up with.  She is great with all sizes of dogs, and she loves cats as well. She does very well with kids too!  She loves to be chased by them in the yard. Her favorite game is "chase me." She does okay on a leash, but would definitely do much better, and adjust so much easier, to a home with a fenced in yard.

At this point I could write a book about this sweet little devil, but I will wrap it but by saying she has some quirks and she will need to be on medication the rest of her life for urinary incontinence, but you won't find a better dog that can make you feel every emotion in one day, lol.

We truly love her and we know her perfect family will find her.

212449123.description:
Meet Jillian! If you are looking for a pup with a ton of personality and a lot of love, then Jillian is your girl.

With big amber eyes and a uniquely painted coat, Jillian is a showstopper. She loves all humans she meets and is a huge sweetheart, but does need continued boundary work as she thinks the best way to let others know she is a fan is to get right up into their personal space! However, she is smart and has picked up on cues and commands very quickly.

Jillian is crate trained and has done well being crated for longer periods of time while her foster is at work. When crated, she tends to do better in a high-traffic area so she can observe what is going on around her and not miss out. While Jillian has not been left alone in the house outside the crate for long periods of time, during shorter bouts, she has done really well and usually just ends up lounging in the living room or sunroom.

Jillian is also potty-trained. She has cleared our 3-foot fence to go after squirrels so is currently on a lead even with a fenced-in backyard. As an almost 2-year-old, Jillian still has a lot of youthful energy and looks forward to going for her walk first thing in the morning. And while she has made a lot of progress over the last few months, Jillian does have a high prey drive and exhibits some excitable reactivity as a result.

Jillian does express high interest in playing with other dogs but will require monitoring as she does not always appropriately read social cues. Slow introductions are best for her.

In just a short amount of time, Jillian has learned both the verbal and nonverbal signals for “sit”, “wait”, “hands in”, “stay” and “lie down”. She transports well and loves her weekly outdoor adventures at Fort Snelling.

Overall, Jillian's ideal home is with an active family or person who is patient, is in a house (she does have a heavy bark!) with a high fenced-in yard. If you are ready for a lively spirit, funny personality, and unconditional companionship - look no further than Jillian!

Meet Buttercup!

Buttercup is a sweet, gentle pup who can be a little shy and reserved when meeting new people, but once she feels safe she becomes very loving and loyal to her people.

Buttercup has low-to-moderate energy and enjoys both playtime and cuddles. She loves playing fetch and will happily bring the ball back so you can throw it again. She’s also extremely treat and food motivated, which makes training fun and rewarding. Belly rubs, snacks, and greeting her people when they come home are some of her favorite things.

She is good with other dogs, but can be reactive when she sees them from a distance and does best with slow introductions. Buttercup doesn’t need another dog in the home, but a calm, friendly dog could help build her confidence.

Buttercup is afraid of men and will need a patient home that allows her time to warm up. Because she isn’t familiar with toddlers, she would do best with older children. She sleeps well in her crate at night and learned potty training quickly.

Buttercup cannot live with cats.

She’s a very sweet, cuddly girl who has clearly had a difficult past and just needs a patient family who will give her the love and security she deserves.

Hi, I'm Norman! My foster mom scooped me up when she heard how I came in to rescue.. I was hanging around the hospital, trying to find some food, when some big dogs came at me and chased me away. Luckily a nice lady who worked there came to help me. I've adjusted to the good life in my foster home really well. There are three other pups here, which I absolutely LOVE! I am learning a lot from the older ones, and I just love to play with the other puppy. My foster mom says my play style is somewhat rough, but I prefer to call it exuberant.

I'm an energetic guy who is always up for an adventure! I am very food motivated and happy to have any snack - even the healthy ones! I eat and sleep in my crate, and occasionally my foster mom will find my hanging out in there by choice! My foster mom tells me her favorite thing about me is my ears, because they are a good mix of floppy and standing up. If you think we might be a good fit, apply to meet me! My foster mom would be happy to tell you all about me!

From my foster mom: Chat GPT estimates that he will be around 50 lbs fully grown, so if you are looking for a pup with the looks of a big dog, but on the smaller side, Norman is for you! I think he would do best in a home with another dog! Both for his happiness, and to allow him to burn some of his boundless energy off easily. He has lived with small children before, and his energy level and love for play chomping did not work out well. He is very sweet and gentle with children when meeting them, but it may be best for him to go to a home with older children only. I am hoping he grows out of some of that, but only time will tell! Norman is a great dog and will be perfect for someone who is very active. When he finally settles down he is a great snuggler!

She's potty trained, will sit by the door when she has to go, good in the bath and car, AMAZING on leash (barely need to hold the leash, no pulling), knows "wait," loves tummy rubs, and is fully vetted, spayed and microchipped. 213593830.description:
Meet Mariska! ❤️

Mariska has been through more than most dogs ever should, but every day she's learning that people can be kind, love can be permanent, and home is a safe place. In 2025, we rescued a litter of her puppies, but we were finally able to rescue her this year. After spending so much of her life surviving and raising babies, this sweet mama is ready to retire, relax, and let someone take care of her for a change.

She's embracing indoor life and making incredible progress. Mariska has discovered the joy of toys and is wonderfully goofy when she plays—leaping, hopping, tossing toys into the air, and catching them herself. She's also incredibly smart! She already knows how to ring the bells to go outside, kennel on cue, sit, leave it, and she's eager to keep learning.

Once Mariska trusts you, she becomes the sweetest little shadow, happily following her favorite person from room to room. A few tasty treats, gentle face scratches, and belly rubs are the fastest way to win her heart. At the end of the day, she's happiest curled up beside you, handing out cuddles and plenty of kisses.

Mariska also enjoys the company of other dogs. She has become friends with every foster dog she's met, but she needs slow, thoughtful introductions and usually takes a day or two to feel comfortable. Because of this, she'd do best in a home that won't expect her to enjoy busy dog parks or daycare settings.

Due to her past, Mariska needs a patient adopter who understands that trust takes time. New people can still be frightening for her, and if she's approached too quickly, she may react out of fear. Her foster family is helping her build confidence, but she'll need someone committed to continuing that journey. For now, she would do best in a home without young children.

When Mariska first entered rescue, she struggled with separation anxiety, barking in her kennel, pawing at the door, or pulling nearby items inside for comfort. She has made tremendous progress, though it's possible some of those behaviors may temporarily return as she adjusts to a new home.

Mariska is looking for someone who will see past her fears and appreciate the incredible dog she's becoming. If you're willing to give her patience, consistency, and unconditional love, she'll reward you with unwavering loyalty, endless affection, and the joy of watching a once-forgotten dog truly blossom into the companion she was always meant to be. ❤️

• My Origin Story: Rescued from under an abandoned shed in Arkansas with my two

brothers.

• My Personality: Sassy, spunky, brave, and completely fearless.

• My Favorite Things: Running outdoors, playing with other dogs, making kid friends, and

As soon as I know you, it is nothing but non-stop butt wiggles and sweet puppy kisses.

Smart Girl Status:

I am learning how to be the best dog ever, and I'm progressing fast:

• Potty Training: I am doing amazing! I prefer to go outdoors. When I'm inside, I use my potty

pads like a pro. The only time I have an accident is when I get super tired.

• Basic Commands: I am practicing my manners and learning commands. My absolute

favorite part of school is getting the treats!

My Dream Family:

I absolutely love other dogs and I love kids! My perfect forever home will have plenty of outdoor

playtime, some fun furry or human siblings, and a family who appreciates a brave girl with a lot of look-at-me attitude.

A few fun facts about me:

I'm a great copilot. I ride beautifully in the car and love tag-alongs.

I've got great manners (mostly!). I am already completely house trained and crate trained. I'm also getting better on my leash walks. I think if you leave reachable food on the counter it's fair game but my foster mom says "not for you" and "down" when I do, so I'm learning to not do that anymore.

My quirks: I love kids, but when I get excited, I still do a little gentle jumping. We are working on it, but I might accidentally startle a really small human! Also, while I'm great at sharing toys and food bowls, I get a little possessive over my special chew bones. I just prefer to enjoy those privately in my crate!

214265511.description:
Tito is suspected to have come to us from a hoarding situation after potentially being bred / a "stud." After a difficult start to life, he is understandably guarded and defensive, and he will need a patient, understanding adopter who is willing to let him build trust at his own pace.

Tito is smart, sassy, independent, and incredibly curious. He’s a bit like a “wisp of smoke”—quick, elusive, and determined to keep all four paws on the ground! He isn’t comfortable being picked up yet, but we’re making progress every day.

He has especially begun to trust his foster mom, choosing to curl up beside her in her recliner. Because of this, we suspect Tito may be more comfortable with women and may need extra time to feel safe around men. He is also gradually warming up to his teenage foster grandsons, showing us that his circle of trust can grow with patience and consistency.

Tito appears to have had little-to-no training before coming into rescue. He is currently pee-pad trained and sleeps quite a bit.

For now, Tito is not a fan of other dogs. He reacts strongly toward the resident dog, so they are kept separated. He is also a significant flight risk and has managed to escape harnesses and take off, so his adopter will need to be extremely careful and use secure, escape-proof equipment and management.

Tito is not going to be an “easy” dog, but he is a worthwhile one. His adopter will need to be committed to giving him time, structure, patience, and plenty of opportunities to learn that the world can be a safe place. In return, they’ll get a smart, savvy, energetic little companion.

Tito is looking for someone who understands that trust isn't given overnight—it’s earned one tiny step at a time. And with Tito, those tiny steps are incredibly rewarding.

214490496.description:
Nos is a timid young adult who is learning to trust people. He takes a bit of time to warm up, but once he has accepted you, he will follow you everywhere. He has attached himself to our 18-year-old son and is thrilled to hang out and snuggle with him.

Once he’s comfortable with you, Nos soaks up the scratches and attention. He loves to nap on the couch, with his head in your lap. He’s even offered a few tentative kisses in the 24 hours we’ve had him.

Nos is just beginning to decompress and gain confidence in life and his environment. He needs people to be slow and patient with him for now. He doesn’t like to feel like he’s being chased or forced to do something - he’d rather think things are his idea. He will go in a crate and hang out a bit, but will bark if you leave him there. He’s happy to explore in our fenced backyard, but it works best if we open the door and let him head out when he’s ready. This will improve in time; he’s had a lot to figure out in a short amount of time.

He’s not yet interested in playing with the other dogs at our house - because they’re not the dogs he’s used to. But he’s been relatively patient with meeting them.

When Nos meets people, he’s more comfortable when they get down to his level (or sit on a couch), rather than tower over him. He will take a slow sniff, then allow you to pet him. After all, he knows he is darling!

Nos is a beautiful boy! He’s got the sweetest chocolate eyes and super soft fur. With time and patience, he will make a great pet!

Lorraine is a beautiful, fun loving youngster who remains fearful of unfamiliar sounds, and sudden movements. She can be a rascal when she feels comfortable and confident as far as checking out what’s on the kitchen counter that may be tasty.

She walks well on a leash as long as her person is alert for squirrels!!

She loves to sit patiently and watch out the window for squirrels. She is not a barker even with those hound dog ears.

Lorraine would do best with another dog in the family to help her feel safe and show her the ropes, and she would benefit from having a fenced in backyard. She enjoys playing chase with any dog willing to run fast, and she likes to wrestle (very quietly) with the foster family’s cattle dog.

She’s not been around cats or young kids.  Pretty sure she would appreciate the more predictable movements of adolescents.

Lorraine can be quite willful when it comes to going in her crate, or putting on her collar to go for a walk. She’s very food motivated so she would thrive in a beginning level obedience class.

She’s a beautiful dog looking for someone who works from home so she doesn’t have to spend a great deal of time in her crate. She sleeps quietly on her own bed next to her foster parents.

Lorraine has faced a truckload of traumas and daunting challenges in her short life. She’s waiting for the right person or family to envelope her with care, structure, and love to help her become her best self. She’s soooo worth the investment of time and energy!

214441275.description:
Tennessee is a sweet, affectionate young pup who is so happy to have a safe place to call home. She has a medium energy level with bursts of puppy enthusiasm and loves playing with toys, spending time with her people, and hanging out with her dog friends. She’s intelligent, eager to learn, and has already shown that she can listen when redirected.

Tennessee is doing well with house training and is currently going potty outside about 90% of the time. Puppy pads by the door help her when she doesn’t quite make it outside. Like many young dogs, she is still working on her manners and can be mouthy and energetic, but she responds well to a firm “no” and will benefit from continued positive training and consistency.

She gets along well with other dogs and would likely love having a young, playful canine companion to help keep her company and burn off some of that puppy energy. The rare time she barks is to try to encourage the older dogs to play with her. She currently sleeps peacefully on a dog bed alongside her foster dog siblings all night.

Tennessee is interested in cats and wants to play with them a little more enthusiastically than they would prefer! With her young age and trainability, she may be able to learn appropriate manners around cats, but a home with dog-savvy cats and a family committed to supervision and training would be best. She has not been tested with young children, so that would be something to consider carefully.

She is also a mouser! She is smart and very alert and has caught a vole and a mouse in the yard.

She is still learning that meals are going to keep coming, and she tends to gobble her food as though she might not get another chance. Slow feeding and consistency should help her learn that she is safe and cared for.

Tennessee doesn’t seem to be a flight risk and appears incredibly grateful to have a home and people who care for her. She’s a young dog with plenty to learn, but underneath that puppy energy is a loving, intelligent girl who is going to make someone an absolutely wonderful companion.

Tennessee would thrive with a family who is ready to give her the structure, training, patience, and love she needs to become her very best self.

214354283.description:
Looking for a spunky, energetic kitten?! Cari is your girl!

When she first arrived, she was pretty sick, but after a quick visit to the vet and the necessary meds, Cari was feeling better almost immediately! It wasn't long before her brave, energetic personality really began to shine! You may notice her right eye looks a little different. This is a temporary effect of the severe upper respiratory infection she had when she arrived in our care, but it should resolve on its own now that Cari has finished her meds and is feeling like a healthy kitten again!

Cari is a very playful and social girl. She loves being around people and even better if they are up for a play session! She is obsessed with her crinkle ball, but can make a toy out of literally anything... whether you like it or not :) This includes fingers and toes... but we are working on redirecting her with actual toys when that happens! For this reason, older children may be a better fit for her. She has even found dog toys to be equally as fun as cat toys! Cari has been living with 3 dogs and 3 cats. She LOVES to play with one of our foster dogs. They have become really great friends! She even likes to nap near him. So safe to say she is dog friendly! She has been very hesitant about meeting the resident cats, but with time and proper introductions, I think she could do well with a friendly, playful feline companion.

Cari plays to her heart's content, which also means she works up quite an appetite! Cari is a huge fan of meal time and doesn't appear to be picky! She loves it all! So no fighting with this one when it comes to choosing what's for dinner. That's a huge win in our book! She also does really well with being picked up and carried. And when she wants to be put down, she will certainly let you know with her  big girl meow! Once and awhile, mainly at bedtime, she will curl up and snuggle with us humans for a little bit which is a real treat.

Cari is the perfect mix of sweet & spunky- and will certainly keep you laughing every day with her crazy, playful antics!

I think Joel would be fine as a solo pet or with another dog in the home who matches his energy and enjoys playing. He seems to have a stronger prey drive, so living with a cat may be difficult. Joel exhibits some classic German Shepherd traits too, including the occasional land shark behavior, so experience with that breed would be helpful.

If you are looking for a best buddy to explore with, Joel could be the perfect dog for you!

Ghost (Little G) is vibing with being the last of his litter to get adopted. Having the human snuggles all for himself has been peak. He still loves to go out and romp around with the foster kids and dogs, but is enjoying coming back in to chill out on the couch post fun run.

He is sleeping through the night in a kennel by himself with some wakeup whines around 5/5:30am for potty time! He is doing great with potty training as long as he is getting let out consistently.

About the Family:

These sweet puppies and their mom were brought into rescue after an emergency surrender situation where they urgently needed a safe landing. Mama Ambrosia is the proud mom of the adorable “Salad Mix” puppies, and her foster family has lovingly called her “Mom". After spending her time raising, loving, and protecting her  nine babies, this sweet girl is finally ready for something she’s never truly had: a forever family of her very own.

Ambrosia is a loving, loyal girl with a big personality and an even bigger heart. She absolutely loves carrying around her favorite toys and soaking up affection. She’s also incredibly smart! In just the few short weeks she’s been in rescue, she has already learned sit, drop it, outside, and shake. She’s eager to learn and continues to make amazing progress every day.

Like any good mama, Ambrosia can be very protective of what she considers valuable. She has some food reactivity and can occasionally become barrier-aggressive when she has food or high-value treats. She has come a long way in just a few weeks, though, and her progress has been wonderful to watch. When she first arrived, she also showed some toy guarding, but she has not demonstrated that behavior recently.

Ambrosia likely could do well with respectful children given her sweet and affectionate personality, but she has not yet been formally tested with kids, so any introductions would need to be thoughtful and supervised.

After giving her puppies the love, protection, and guidance they needed, she deserves the chance to be someone's baby now. She’s ready for a family who will continue to help her grow, celebrate her progress, and show her just how wonderful life can be.

If you're looking for a loyal companion, a smart girl with plenty of personality, and a best friend who has a whole lot of love left to give, Ambrosia is ready to meet you.

Yuki is a gentle, good-natured and smart girl. She is potty trained. In her previous home she learned to ring a bell when she wanted to go outside. She is kennel trained, but definitely prefers to be right by your side. She is the best friend you always wanted.

Yuki can be skittish in a new environment, therefore she would love a patient family that will allow her to get comfortable at her own pace. A calm and predictable home with kids 12 and up would be best for her. Chaos can be to overwhelming to her.

Her ideal home would include the following:

Walking and squeaky tennis balls are an absolute must! She is an enthusiastic walker! She pulls a bit to begin with. She wants to get all the smells in, but she will settle down after a short time. Chasing and squeaking her tennis ball is a favorite pastime.

A fenced yard to chase that ball and show off her zoomies.

Yuki really enjoys chasing the cats. While she hasn’t been allowed to get very close to them, living with cats may not be a successful fit.

Calmer dogs only. Yuki does not enjoy dogs that get in her face. If there is another dog in your home, it would need to be a more laid-back pup. She will need a slow, safe introduction to her new sibling.

A window to observe the outside world. She likes to lay in the sun and see the goings on in the neighborhood.

Though she has her playful and adventurous side, sitting beside you on the couch is her favorite way to wrap up the day. If you are a looking for the ultimate companion Yuki is your girl. She is excited to meet you!

Sonia can be tentative at first, but once she feels comfortable, her affectionate personality shines and she shows what an incredible companion she can be. She loves going for walks and does well on a leash without pulling or reacting to other dogs. Curious about every sound and bit of neighborhood wildlife, she may weave a little or pause unexpectedly to take in an interesting sight or sound.

At home, Sonia is quiet and relaxed with the resident dog and two cats. Although the cats needed a little extra time to warm up to her, Sonia has been gentle and respectful and does not chase them; they now get along well.

She is house-trained and has not been heard barking in her foster home. Like many dogs adjusting to a new routine, Sonia is still learning not to jump up on visitors, sample food that isn’t hers, or investigate the counters. With patience, consistency, and the stability of a loving home, she will continue building confidence and blossom into a wonderful companion.

Are you looking for an energetic companion who can do 5ft box jumps, has the speed and agility of a professional athlete, and the ability to inhale food like a competitive eater? Dell is your guy!

He greets every exciting thing, from walks, meal time, or just getting to greet you, with 5ft vertical leaps of joy. He enjoys playing with the young resident dog and gladly demonstrates his quick turns of speed when they chase around the yard.

Dell is extremely food motivated. He uses a slow feeder to prevent him from eating his meals in 2.7 seconds flat, and will gladly hoover your kitchen floor for anything that drops.

Dell is kennel trained, staying quiet while he is kenneled unless he hears others having fun. He is also housebroken, with only a couple of accidents his first few days in the foster home.

Dell gets along with dogs, cats, and kids, but older kids are recommended so he doesn't use really young ones as a spring board to reach greater heights. He knows "sit", "kennel", and responds very well to a curt "no" to dissuade him from naughty behaviors.

Dell would thrive in an active home with another young dog for a playmate, or with someone who is interested in dog activities (fly ball, agility, disc work, etc). Because he is so food motivated, training should be a breeze.

Simon is still learning that people can be trusted, but he’s making progress every day. With patience, gentle encouragement, and plenty of treats, he’s slowly gaining confidence and learning that people can be pretty wonderful.

He’s also working hard on his house training and continuing to learn all the things that come with being a puppy. He isn’t much of a barker, but when he does find his voice, get ready for the cutest little puppy bark you’ve ever heard!

One thing to know about Simon is that being picked up isn’t his favorite. We’re working on this with positive reinforcement, treats, and plenty of positive experiences at his own pace. Because he’s still building trust and confidence, Simon will do best with older, respectful children who understand the importance of giving him space and letting him come around on his own terms.

Simon is a sweet, playful, curious boy with so much potential. He’ll need a family willing to give him a little extra patience as he learns to trust, but watching him grow into a confident, loving companion will be so rewarding.

214567711.description:
Hello! I’m Petey Wheatie and I am an extra special girl looking for an extra special forever home.

In late September, I had a vet appointment and found that my glaucoma was so severe, and causing me so much pain, that both my eyes needed to be removed. I also had much needed dental work done to remove several infected teeth. I am no longer in pain, but it’s been quite an adjustment losing my sight.

While I couldn’t see well before, the complete loss of my vision has been a big adjustment. I am still a very happy girl who loves people and I especially love the quiet safety of my foster mom’s lap while she works.

While I currently live with dogs and a cat, I am easily startled by movement and noise, and can be territorial with my favorite spots, and would do best as an only dog/animal in a home without children and or a lot activity.

True to my breed, I am a vocal girl and like to communicate when I am excited, wanting attention, lonely, or feeling protective.

I much prefer to be with people and would be a great companion for a retired person or a home where my parent/s are home more than away.

I am reliably house trained, love treats, cuddling, burrowing under covers, am a very good sleeper, and am very excited by the short walks I’ve been able to take since my recovery.

Because I’m such a special girl, I will need a special home where my parent(s) are patient, willing to help me navigate my world, and are willing to make my immediate environment safe and accessible for me. If that sounds like you, apply today!

I’m currently being fostered on a hobby farm, and let me tell you, I’m loving everything about it! There’s so much to see, smell, and explore, and I’m enjoying all the new adventures that come with farm life.

I’m doing wonderfully with my puppy manners, too! I’m kennel trained, housetrained, and even doing well on a leash. I’m a smart little girl who’s ready to keep learning as I grow!

I get along with other dogs and even do well with kittens, so I could be a great addition to a home with furry friends. Whether it’s playtime with my buddies, chasing after my favorite toys, or curling up for some quality cuddle time, I’m happiest when I’m surrounded by love.

Since I’m still a young puppy, I’ll need a family who can continue helping me learn and grow with patience, consistency, and lots of positive reinforcement. I’ll need all the usual puppy care, guidance, and socialization to help me become the very best girl I can be!

I’m looking for a forever family who will give me a safe, loving home and include me in all life’s adventures. Could that be you?

Meet Scarlett! This sweet little girl is the definition of a princess who lives for the GOOD life!

Scarlett is a shy girl who may take a little time to warm up, but once she feels safe, you’ll have a best friend for life. She enjoys other dogs, but she’ll need time and patience to adjust. We think she would truly thrive as the only dog in the home, where she can soak up all the love and attention her heart desires.

A few things to love about Scarlett:

🐾 Fully potty trained

🐾 Leash trained (although she’d much rather be carried!)

🐾 Loves her toys

🐾 Feels safe and comfortable in her kennel

🐾 Has the sweetest little personality

🐾 May jump up occasionally, but it’s only because she’s trying to give you hugs!

Let’s be honest — Scarlett is NOT the girl you take on long walks. She’s the girl who will try to climb straight into your arms and convince you that carrying her everywhere is the only acceptable option. Her foster mom has pretty much accepted her role as Scarlett’s personal chauffeur!

Her dream life? A pup cup, a warm seat in the front passenger seat, a cozy place to relax, and the occasional belly rub. She’s a front-seat princess through and through!

Scarlett may be shy at first, but underneath that timid exterior is a girl who just wants to feel safe, loved, and included. She’s waiting for someone who will be patient with her, let her blossom at her own pace, and show her just how wonderful life can be.

Someone out there is going to be one VERY lucky human. Scarlett is just waiting for her person — her safe place, her favorite lap, and her forever sidekick. 🩷

Potty training is going GREAT! I’m learning my routine and doing really well! I still have an accident here and there, but hey, I’m just a baby! Give me a little patience and consistency, and I’ll keep learning.

Great with kids of all ages! I love my little human friends! I do have normal puppy nibbles and biting that we’re working on, so I’ll need my family to keep helping me learn good puppy manners.

Doggy-approved! I love other dogs and would be happy to have some furry friends to play with!

Cat enthusiast… maybe a little TOO enthusiastic! I enjoy picking on the kitty, so I’ll need a family willing to help me learn respectful kitty boundaries and supervise our interactions.

I’m a good boy with a big personality, a clever little brain, and a heart full of love. I’m still a puppy, so I’ll need a family ready for all the fun, training, patience, and occasional chaos that comes with raising a little guy like me!

All I need now is someone to call MY PERSON, a cozy place to sleep, and a family who will love me forever.

Meet Luna:

Luna is an incredibly wonderful pup that is potty trained, crate trained, and very independent. Luna has a love for her “person”. Luna would do best with an owner that wants a “shadow” and a low energy dog. Luna is 50% cattle dog, 10% husky, 10% chow chow. * *luna has a history of being aggressive and biting other resident dogs over food, toys, and her people*

America is a mixed-breed female puppy with some pretty adorable German Shepherd physical and personality traits. And those ears!?!!

America is also the social butterfly of her litter. She loves everyone, gets along with dogs of all sizes, and believes the best place to be is wherever the action is happening!

This girl is all about the good things in life: toys, bones, a comfy bed, a full food bowl, and a water dish that’s always ready when she needs a pit stop. Add in some playtime with her dog friends and quality time with her people, and she is living her very best puppy life!

She’s already showing off some impressive skills like mastering going up and down the stairs and she’s starting to work on her potty training. She hasn’t needed a kennel in her foster home because she and her siblings have their own gated area and playpen. When she’s ready to come out and join the fun, she’ll let you know! Otherwise, her noise-making includes the occasional adorable snoring during nap time.

America is still a puppy, so she’ll need a family ready to help her learn, grow, and navigate all the adventures life has in store. With her outgoing personality, love of other dogs, and desire to be part of the family, she’s sure to bring plenty of fun and laughter to her forever home.

214734105.description:
Gushers is a mixed-breed male puppy with some pretty strong German Shepherd looks and personality! This handsome little guy came into rescue on the shy side, but he’s discovering that the world isn’t quite so scary after all. Every day, he’s growing a little braver, a little bolder, and a whole lot more curious!

Gushers is good with dogs of all sizes, although those big, booming barks can still send him looking for a safe place to hide. He’s a sensitive soul who just needs a little patience, encouragement, and time to figure things out. And when that curiosity kicks in? That’s when the fun begins!

One of his most adorable features is his ears. Seriously, those things have a mind of their own! They swivel in different directions like furry little antennae, and the expressions he makes while trying to figure out the world around him are absolutely priceless.

Like any growing puppy, Gushers has a list of favorite things: toys, bones, cozy blankets, yummy food, and lots of fresh water. He’s working on mastering the stairs, loves playing under the bed, and is just getting started with potty training both outdoors and on potty pads.

Gushers hasn’t spent time in a kennel at his foster home. He and his siblings have a gated area and puppy pen to call their own, and when he’s ready to come out, he lets you know! In fact, for being a little shy at times, he’s surprisingly the most vocal of his siblings. Apparently, he has plenty to say once he feels comfortable! We take that as a win!

Gushers will need a family willing to let him blossom at his own pace. A patient, loving home that celebrates the little victories will help him continue building confidence and discovering just how wonderful life can be. Another confident, friendly dog could be a great companion for him, provided introductions and interactions are a good fit.

If you have room in your heart for a sweet boy who just needs a little time to shine, Gushers might be your perfect match!

He’s got the ears, he’s got the personality, and he’s got a whole lot of sweetness waiting to burst out.

214734109.description:
Ring Pop is a mixed-breed female puppy with some beautiful German Shepherd features and a tender little heart that’s learning to trust. When Ring Pop first came into rescue, the world felt like a pretty big, scary place. New people, new sounds, and new experiences were all a little overwhelming for this timid girl. But every single day, she’s finding a little more courage. She’s learning that kind hands are safe, that new experiences don’t always have to be scary, and that just maybe this big world has some pretty wonderful things waiting for her.

Ring Pop has already identified a few of her favorite parts of courageous puppy life! Toys, bones, cozy blankets... sign her up! Mealtime and water breaks...two paws up! And she is learning all kinds of new things, including how to navigate stairs and the beginnings of potty training. She hasn’t spent time in a kennel at her foster home because she and her siblings have a gated area and puppy pen of their own.

She’s also a pretty quiet little lady. If something worries her, you might hear the tiniest little whine - a soft, sweet way of letting you know she’s not quite sure about things yet. She loves other dogs, but those extra-loud, big barks can still send her searching for a safe hiding spot. She’s learning to navigate the world at her own pace, and we’re helping her discover that she can be brave without having to do everything all at once.

Ring Pop isn’t the puppy who will demand all your attention the moment you walk through the door. She’s the girl who needs you to be patient enough to earn her trust, gentle enough to respect her fears, and loving enough to celebrate every tiny victory along the way.

Her forever family will need to understand that confidence takes time. She’ll benefit from a calm, predictable environment, plenty of positive encouragement, and the freedom to approach new experiences at her own pace. In return, you’ll have the privilege of watching a timid little puppy discover her own strength and personality.

This girl deserves all the things every puppy deserves. A soft place to land. A family who thinks she’s wonderful. Adventures when she’s ready. A lifetime of safety, snuggles, and unconditional love. Her foster knows that one Ring Pop knows she’s safe at home, her love will be the sweetest gift of all.

214734182.description:
Hi hi hi!! I’m Tater, your future bestie, professional toy destroyer, and part-time landshark! I’m a teeny tiny puppy, and FULL of personality. I love playing with my toys, exploring outside, and getting all the cuddles I can possibly fit into my day. My foster mom says I’m the more rambunctious one, but I so much love to give.

I’m still working on my potty training and learning that fingers and toes are NOT chew toys (rude, I know), but my foster mom is helping me learn to redirect my puppy bites to my toys. I’m a very smart, food-motivated little guy, so treats are definitely the way to my heart!

I’m also VERY interested in becoming best friends with my foster mom’s resident cat. They haven’t quite realized how amazing I am yet, but I’m working on it.

At bedtime, I do great in my crate with my brother, where we snuggle up together all night. I haven’t tried sleeping alone yet, but honestly, my dream is to be your little bed buddy.

Because I’m SO little, I have ramps to safely get on and off the couch to protect my tiny body. I could potentially do well in a family with respectful children, but because I’m still learning not to nip and I’m so teeny tiny, I’ll need gentle handling and supervision around little ones.

If you’re looking for a tiny best friend who will make you laugh, keep you entertained, and then melt into your arms for a cuddle, I might just be your guy.

Love,

Tater  🐾

Well hello there! I’m Tot, a pocket-sized puppy & sweetheart with a BIG personality packed into a very tiny body. I love my toys, playing outside, and spending time with my favorite people. But my absolute FAVORITE thing? CUDDLES.

When I get sleepy, I’ll come find you, snuggle right into your neck, and melt into the tiniest little cuddle puddle you’ve ever seen. My foster mom says it’s pretty much impossible not to fall in love with me.

I’m the more submissive one between me and my brother Tater, but don’t let that fool you. I also happen to be part kangaroo! When I want your attention, I’ll jump straight up with all my might. I’m so tiny that I barely go anywhere, but I promise I’m giving it my absolute best effort!

I’m still working on my potty training and learning that people’s fingers and toes aren’t chew toys. I’m in my little landshark era, but my foster mom is helping me learn to chew on my toys instead. I’m also very food motivated, so treats make learning extra fun!

At night, I do great in my crate with my brother, and we snuggle together until morning. I haven’t tried sleeping by myself yet, but I would LOVE to be your little bed buddy someday. Why sleep alone when you could have a tiny Tot tucked into your neck?

I’m VERY tiny, so I have ramps to help me safely get on and off the couch. I could potentially do well with respectful children, but because I’m so small and still in my puppy biting stage, I’ll need gentle handling and supervision around little ones.

If your dream is a little shadow who follows you around, jumps for your attention, and snuggles into your neck when he’s sleepy, I think we might be a perfect match. I have a whole lot of love to give, and I’m just waiting for my forever person to give it to.

Love and tiny kangaroo hops,

Tot 🐾

I'm a low-to-medium energy pup - with those occasional puppy-like zoomies when outside or after a nice nap (those naps really re-charge my batteries...but my zoomies deplete those batteries rather quick, and I'm back to my mellow cuddly self).

I am working on crate training, though I have been a perfect angel being able to free roam - no shoes have become a casualty! I love sleeping with my people, but when I do get warm, I will go to my bed in my crate or on the couch.

I am potty trained and have had no issues with accidents during 'normal' working hours (even while free-roaming).

I am sharing a space with 3 other dogs, and as long as I have slow introductions, and a few days to decompress, I am really good with other dogs. I know 'sit' and 'shake' and my Foster Mom will be working with me on how to walk like a good girl on a leash.

I'm also a very quiet gal, no whining or barking, so I'd be good in any sort of home.

*Originated from: South Dakota Reservation.

Elvis isperfection rolled into a little floof. He likes to snuggle up and give gentle little kisses. He barely makes a peep unless he feels he’s been left in an unjust situation, he will quickly let you know, but it doesn’t last long. Even though he’s just a baby, he seems to be getting the hang of that tricky potty training and he doesn’t mind being in the kennel too much.

He likes to be at his foster mom’s feet or playing with one of the other dogs in the house. Then he will just find a spot to go take a nap when he gets bored. He’s great with kids or really, anyone he meets, so we imagine at this age, he would be just fine with cats as well. He may try to play, but he plays very gently and knows when to back away. Elvis would make the perfect addition to any home!

214806973.description:
Meet Titos: a big sweetheart with a tiny body, a big heart, and just the right amount of diva energy.

Titos favorite place is wherever you are. He’ll happily follow you from room to room, supervise your daily activities, and then settle into a cozy spot nearby while he waits for his next cuddle opportunity. He’s a pretty low-key guy who enjoys the quieter side of life, making him a great fit for apartment living or a home with someone who’s retired or works from home. The one exception to his quiet nature? Hearing another dog barking nearby. Tito takes his neighborhood watch duties seriously.

He seems to be fully potty-trained, though he may occasionally sneak off to handle business if it’s been a while since his last potty break. He’s not a fan of the crate, but he does wonderfully free-roaming while you’re away. No dramatic protests or home renovations here; just a little guy finding the comfiest spot to nap until you get back.

Titos foster mom tortured him with a bath once, (and he hated it), but did appreciate being clean afterwards. He did not mind getting his nails clipped, though!

He may occasionally eat from his bowl like a normal dog, but he’d much rather be hand-fed by his personal chef (that’s you). Honestly, he knows what he deserves.

His foster home includes two dogs (a 7-year-old medium-sized dog and a 5-month-old small-to-medium puppy) and a well-behaved 8-year-old cat. Tito generally coexists peacefully with the dogs, though he can get a little protective of his people when the larger dog comes around. Cats, on the other hand, are apparently perfectly acceptable cuddle companions. He has no issues with his feline foster sibling and is happy to snuggle up right beside her.

Because Titos can be a bit territorial around larger dogs, he’ll do best in a home with no other dogs, or one with smaller or younger canine companions who are a good match for his personality. A cat-friendly home could also be right up his alley!

So, if you’re looking for a loyal little shadow, a professional cuddle buddy, a part-time hand-feeding enthusiast, and a tiny security guard who takes his job very seriously (but would also like a nap afterward), Tito might just be your guy. He’s ready to bring a whole lot of love to the lucky person who makes him part of their family.

214734095.description:
Looking for a laid-back best friend with a little bit of personality? Meet Halloween, a handsome husky mix with a stunning brindle coat, soft thick fur, and a heart as sweet as can be.

Like many husky mixes, Halloween has plenty to say and isn't shy about sharing his thoughts with you! Whether he's greeting you when you get home or commenting on the days' events, his adorable "talking" is guaranteed to make you smile.

Halloween is affectionate and easygoing with a low-to-medium energy level. He's always up for a good nap, but when it's playtime, he's happy to join the fun with his dog friends. He gets along well with both large and small dogs and has excellent canine manners.

He's also cat-friendly, although he occasionally thinks it's fun to chase them for a quick game. Around children, Halloween is patient and gentle, though he's more of a calm companion than an active playmate.

This smart boy is both housetrained and kennel trained, making him an easy addition to your home. He especially loves chew toys and can often be found happily entertaining himself with his favorite toy.

If you're looking for a loyal companion who combines cuddles, conversation, and just the right amount of playfulness, Halloween may be the perfect match. He' ready to find his forever home!

214734134.description:
Stuffing is proving to be one smart little guy! This sweet boy is off to a great start and is already showing what a wonderful addition he could be to a loving family.

- Dog-friendly: He gets along well with other dogs.

- Cat-friendly: He does well with cats, too!

- Kid-friendly: He’s good with children.

- A smart cookie: Stuffing already knows how to sit and lie down, and he seems eager to learn even more!

- Making great progress: He’s doing well with potty training and is learning his nighttime routine.

- Crate training success: Stuffing sleeps in his crate at night and settles down after just a few minutes.

Stuffing is a little guy with so much potential! With patience, consistency, and lots of love, he’s sure to keep blossoming into a wonderful companion.

Could Stuffing be the missing piece of your family? He’s looking for a forever home where he can continue learning, growing, and being loved for the special pup he is!

Who’s ready to give Stuffing a forever home?
